description.narrative: This project, targeting 1,446 smallholder sesame growers (38% female and 8% living with disabilities) from 4 Wards (13, 14, 15 and 16) in Mwenezi district, is a continuation of a previous initiative that was supported by Christian Aid – Strengthening Household Resilience and Incomes in Mwenezi through the Promotion of Sesame (SHRIMPS). The main focus of SHRIMPS-2 is to strengthen governance systems in the MSGCS and to strengthen the active and meaningful participation of the MSGCS in the affairs of SesAfrika (Pvt) Limited, a company in which the cooperative has a shareholding of 24.5%. SesAfrika is a sesame value addition business that was established by SAT last year, with support from Christian Aid who provided funding for sesame processing equipment and sheds. Capacity strengthening: In strengthening the capacity of the MSGCS, SAT will roll out a series of training workshops tailored to meet pre-identified training needs of the cooperative. The training workshops will be conducted in close collaboration with the Ministry of Women Affairs, SMEs and Cooperative Development (MWASMECD) in Mwenezi district. Strengthening the capacity of the MSGCS is critical in many ways, not least in amplifying the voice of smallholder sesame growers and diluting the influence of middlemen on the sesame market in the district. A stronger MSGCS will have appropriate policies, procedures and systems, trained and confident leaders who are able to negotiate sound business deals and represent their members, and good connections with credible sesame offtake markets. Promote access to water: using clean energy: An additional project component is around improved access to clean and safe water for hundreds of households (xx males: xx females) in Ward 13. This intervention will reduce the risk of exposure to water-borne diseases and the significant burden that women and girls carry in collecting water for their households, including the risk to violence. Besides the solarized borehole in Ward 13, SAT will also facilitate the establishment and strengthening of the capacity of a Water Point Management Committee (WPMC) tasked to manage the new facility and to mobilize community support for the maintenance of the borehole in future. Collaboration and layering: Christian Aid Zimbabwe will provide £25,000 for the project. In implementing this initiative, SAT will also leverage support from the AICS-funded SEFF project and OAK Foundation-funded Youth Vocational Skills Training Programme, which are both being implemented by SAT in Mwenezi district.
